paragraphs: Overview – Lakeland Fire + Safety is a global provider of quality safety products that protect the world's workers, first responders, and communities during the most critical situations. The Company's products, which are governed by rigorous safety standards and regulations, are used to either protect the wearer from their environment or protect a product or process from the wearer in a broad range of markets around the world, including chemical, clean room, energy, fire service, manufacturing, and utility applications. Lakeland's product portfolio includes firefighter protective apparel and accessories, high-end chemical protective suits, limited use/disposable protective clothing, durable woven garments, high performance FR/AR apparel, and high visibility clothing. On March 27, 2026, the Company sold its high performance FR/AR apparel and high visibility clothing line to National Safety Apparel. For additional information, please see Note 14 to our consolidated financial statements.

Lakeland Fire + Safety's fiscal year 2026 reflected continued progress in advancing our strategy to build a comprehensive portfolio of protective products and services across both our Fire Services and Industrial product lines. During the year, we completed two acquisitions that expanded our advanced decontamination, inspection and repair service capabilities for firefighting garments, further strengthening our Fire Services platform. While we believe we now have the full suite of premier global head-to-toe fire services, we expect to move forward by continuing to implement strategies to accelerate growth and margins by continuing our acquisition focus on the fire turnout gear industry. We continue to see growth opportunities in the fire and industrial space. We have grown our revenue year-over-year and demonstrated our success with our recent acquisitions, providing confidence in our roll-up strategy, and we now have ample capital and flexibility to execute this strategy.

The Company's strong market position across its focus product categories and markets is supported by continued and increasing investment in its global footprint, particularly owning and operating its own manufacturing facilities, acquiring complementary companies or products that expand and enhance product offerings and/or geographic customer territories and investing in sales and marketing resources in countries around the world. We believe that ownership of manufacturing is the keystone to building a resilient supply chain and providing high-quality products to our customers. Having nine manufacturing locations in eight countries on five continents, and sourcing core raw materials from multiple suppliers in various countries affords Lakeland with superior manufacturing capabilities and supply chain resilience compared to our competitors who use contractors. Additionally, our focus on providing customers with best-in-class service includes the strategic location of our sales team members.
Lakeland is committed to protecting the world's workers, first responders, and communities while creating shareholder value. Key elements of our corporate strategy include:
• Creating a high-performance culture driven by our corporate values, • Investing resources in high-growth geographies and product categories,
• Building a premier global firefighter safety brand through product and marketing enhancements,

• Driving profitable growth in high-end chemical and limited-use/disposable protective clothing through product development, strategic pricing initiatives, channel diversification, and operations optimization, and
• Acquiring companies that improve Lakeland's competitive advantage in focus markets.

On September 15, 2025, the Company acquired 100% of U.S.-based Arizona PPE Recon, Inc. ("Arizona PPE") for cash consideration of approximately $4.1 million. Founded in 2016, Arizona PPE is a leading UL-certified independent services provider ("ISP") for performing advanced decontamination, inspection and repairs on firefighting garments for the Arizona market, as well as providing educational and training classes to fire departments and personnel to help them implement and adhere to NFPA 1851 guidelines.

On September 15, 2025, the Company acquired 100% of U.S.-based California PPE Recon, Inc. ("California PPE") for a combination of approximately $2.4 million in cash consideration and 227,728 unregistered shares of the Company's common stock with an estimated fair value of $3.3 million at the date of acquisition, subject to post-closing adjustments and customary holdback provisions. Founded in 2022, California PPE is a leading and rapidly expanding UL-certified ISP in the California firefighting services market, one of the largest fire markets in the U.S. It also provides advanced decontamination, repair, and inspection of firefighting personal protective equipment, along with rental services and sales of cleaning detergents, extractors, and dryers.

On December 16, 2024, the Company acquired U.S. based Veridian Limited ("Veridian") for cash consideration of approximately $26.3 million subject to post-closing adjustments and customary holdback provisions. Founded in 1992, Veridian is a leading provider of firefighter protective apparel, including fire and rescue garments, gloves and boots and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa.

On July 1, 2024, the Company acquired the fire and rescue business of LHD Group Deutschland GmbH and its subsidiaries in Hong Kong and Australia (collectively, "LHD") in an all-cash transaction. Total consideration was $14.8 million, net of $1.5 million cash acquired, of which $15.5 million was paid to retire LHD's debt and $0.8 million was paid to the seller at closing. LHD is a leading provider of firefighter turnout gear, accessories, and personal protective equipment cleaning, repair, and maintenance and is headquartered in Wesseling, Germany, with operations in Hong Kong and Australia.

On February 5, 2024, the Company acquired Italy and Romania-based Jolly Scarpe S.p.A. and Jolly Scarpe Romania S.R.L. (collectively, "Jolly") in an all-cash transaction. Total consideration was valued at $9.0 million. Jolly is a leading designer and manufacturer of professional footwear for the firefighting, military, police, and rescue markets. The company is headquartered in Montebelluna, Italy, with manufacturing operations in Bucharest, Romania.

Segments – The Company has seven revenue-generating reportable geographic segments under ASC Topic 280 "Segment Reporting": USA Operations, Other Foreign, Europe, Mexico, Asia, Canada, and Latin America. Segment Reporting is presented in Note 14 – Segment Information of the consolidated financial statements in Part II Item 8 of this Form 10-K. Because our consolidated financial statements are stated in U.S. dollars and much of our business is conducted outside the U.S., currency fluctuations may affect our results of operations and financial position and may affect the comparability of our results between financial periods.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Industry

We are subject to risk as a result of our international manufacturing operations, including risks resulting from recent developments in the international trade environment, such as increased import tariffs.
A terrorist attack or other geopolitical crisis could negatively impact our domestic and/or international operations.
Our results of operations may vary widely from quarter to quarter.
Disruption in our supply chain, manufacturing or distribution operations could adversely affect our business.
Climate change and other sustainability matters may adversely affect our business and operations.

Pandemics or disease outbreaks, such as COVID-19, may cause unfavorable economic or market conditions, which could impact demand patterns and/or disrupt global supply chains and manufacturing operations.
Because we do not have long-term commitments from many of our customers, we must estimate customer demand, and errors in our estimates could negatively impact our inventory levels and net sales.
The markets we compete in are highly competitive, and some of our competitors have greater financial and other resources than we do.
Our operations are substantially dependent upon key personnel.
Technological change could negatively affect sales of our products and our performance.
Cybersecurity incidents could disrupt business operations, result in the loss of critical and confidential information and adversely impact our reputation and results of operations.
Our success depends in part on our proprietary technology, and if we fail to successfully obtain or enforce our intellectual property rights, our competitive position may be harmed.

Our inability to successfully identify, consummate and integrate current and future acquisitions and strategic investments or to realize anticipated cost savings and other benefits could adversely affect our business.

We are implementing a new enterprise resource planning system, and challenges with the implementation of the system or further delays may impact our internal control over financial reporting, business and operations.
We have recognized impairment charges in the past, and we may be required to recognize additional impairment charges in the future, including for goodwill and other intangible assets.
Financial Risks
Our results of operations could be negatively affected by potential fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates.
Covenants in our credit facilities may restrict our financial and operating flexibility.
We may need additional funds, and if we are unable to obtain these funds, we may not be able to expand or operate our business as planned.
Legal and Regulatory Risks
We are subject to certain U.S. and foreign anti-corruption laws and other laws and regulations as a result of our international operations.

We are subject to various U.S. and foreign tax laws, and any changes in these laws related to the taxation of businesses and resolutions of tax disputes could adversely affect our results of operations.
We may be subject to product liability claims, and insurance coverage could be inadequate or unavailable to cover these claims.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risks before investing in our common stock. The risks and uncertainties described below are those that we have identified as material, but they are not the only risks that we may face. If any of the events referred to below actually occur, our business, financial condition, liquidity and results of operations could suffer. In that case, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment. In addition, the risks discussed below include forward-looking statements, and our actual results may differ substantially from those discussed in the forward-looking statements. See the section titled "Information Relating to Forward-Looking Statements" for a discussion of such statements and their limitations. You should also refer to the other information in this Form 10-K and in the documents we incorporate by reference into this Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and the related notes.

Because most of our products are manufactured at our facilities located in China, Vietnam, Mexico, Argentina, New Zealand, Romania and India, our operations are subject to risks inherent in doing business internationally. Such risks include the adverse effects on operations from corruption, war, international terrorism, civil disturbances, political instability, trade wars, government activities such as border taxes and renegotiation of treaties, deprivation of contract and property rights and currency valuation changes. Based on the complex relationships between China and the U.S., there is an inherent risk that political, diplomatic, military, or other events could result in business disruptions, including increased regulatory enforcement against companies, tariffs, trade embargoes, and export restrictions.

In recent years, the U.S. has imposed tariffs on various products imported into the U.S. These tariffs have resulted in, and may continue to trigger, retaliatory actions by affected countries, including the imposition of tariffs on the U.S. by other countries. Under the current administration, trade policy has been a central focus, with renewed scrutiny on trade relationships with China and efforts to renegotiate or withdraw from key agreements such as the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). This shift has included the introduction of additional tariffs, including on Mexican, Canadian, Chinese, Vietnamese, European Union and Indian goods, targeted sanctions, and restrictions on investments linked to industries deemed critical to U.S. national security. Certain foreign governments, such as China, Canada, Mexico and the European Union, have instituted or are considering imposing trade sanctions on certain U.S. goods and denying U.S. companies access to critical raw materials.

The extent and duration of increased tariffs, which we are unable to predict, and the resulting impact on general economic conditions and on our business are uncertain and depend on various factors, such as negotiations between the U.S. and affected countries, the responses of other countries or regions, exemptions or exclusions that may be granted, availability and cost of alternative sources of supply, and demand for our products in affected markets. For example, after announcing proposed blanket tariff rates of 46% on imports from Vietnam in April 2025, the U.S. and Vietnam governments announced a trade deal between the countries that imposes 20% tariffs on all products imported to the U.S. from Vietnam that became effective on August 7, 2025. On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling striking down certain tariffs previously imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA") but did not address potential refunds for tariffs paid under IEEPA. The ultimate availability, timing, and amount of any potential refunds of such tariffs remain highly uncertain and are subject to further legal, regulatory, and administrative developments. After the Supreme Court's ruling, the Trump Administration immediately imposed new global tariffs pursuant to Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows for tariffs of up to 15% for a period of up to 150 days, and indicated its intention to consider other legal options for imposing tariffs.

Our business has been negatively affected by the IEEPA tariffs and may be negatively affected in the future by this quickly evolving tariff situation and the economic uncertainty created thereby. Tariffs increase the cost of our products and the components and raw materials that go into making them. These increased costs adversely impact the gross margin we earn on our products. Tariffs have also increased the cost of our products for customers, making them less competitive and have resulted in reduced consumer demand. Countries may also adopt other measures, such as controls on imports or exports of goods, technology, or data, that could adversely impact the Company's operations and supply chain and limit the Company's ability to offer our products and services as designed. These measures can require us to take various actions, including changing suppliers, shifting production of certain products to lower-tariff countries and restructuring business relationships. Changing our operations in accordance with new or changed trade restrictions can be expensive, time-consuming, and disruptive to our operations, as well as distracting to management. Such restrictions have been, and may be in the future, announced, amended, paused, reinstated, or rescinded with little or no advance notice, and we may not be able to effectively mitigate all adverse impacts from such measures. Uncertainty surrounding trade and other international disputes has had a negative effect on consumer confidence and spending, and we cannot predict how long such uncertainty may last. These events have reduced customer demand, and additional tariff policies could exacerbate those effects, increase the cost of our products and services, or otherwise have a materially adverse impact on our customers' and suppliers' businesses and results of operations, which could in turn additionally adversely impact our financial performance and growth prospects.

Our global operations are susceptible to global events, including acts or threats of war or terrorism, international conflicts, political instability, and natural disasters. The occurrence or continuation of any of these events could have an adverse effect on our business results and financial condition.

paragraphs: You should read the following summary together with the more detailed business information and consolidated financial statements and related notes that appear elsewhere in this Form 10-K and in the documents that we incorporate by reference into this Form 10-K. This document may contain certain "forward-looking" information within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. This information involves risks and uncertainties. Our actual results may differ materially from the results discussed in the forward-looking statements. In this Form 10-K, (a) "FY" means fiscal year; thus for example, FY26 refers to the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, and (b) "Q" refers to a quarter; thus, for example, Q4 FY26 refers to the fourth quarter of the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026.

Lakeland Industries, Inc. and Subsidiaries, doing business as "Lakeland Fire + Safety" ("Lakeland," the "Company," "we," "our" or "us"), manufacture and sell a comprehensive line of fire services and industrial protective clothing and accessories for the industrial and first responder markets. In addition, we provide decontamination, repair and rental services that complement our fire services portfolio. Our products are sold globally by our in-house sales teams, our customer service group, and authorized independent sales representatives to a strategic and selective global network of authorized distribution partners. Our authorized distributors supply end users across various industries, including integrated oil, chemical/petrochemical, automobile, transportation, steel, glass, construction, smelting, cleanroom, janitorial, pharmaceutical and high-tech electronics manufacturers, as well as scientific, medical laboratories and the utilities industry. We also supply federal, state and local governmental agencies and departments, including fire and law enforcement, airport crash rescue units, the Department of Defense, the Department of Homeland Security and the Centers for Disease Control. Internationally, we sell to a mix of end-users directly and to industrial distributors, depending on the particular country and market. In addition to the United States (U.S.), sales are made into more than 50 foreign countries, the majority of which were into China, the European Economic Community ("EEC"), Canada, Chile, Argentina, Russia, Kazakhstan, Colombia, Mexico, Ecuador, India, Uruguay, Middle East, Southeast Asia, Australia, Hong Kong and New Zealand.
We had net sales of $192.6 million in FY26 and $167.2 million in FY25.

We have operated facilities in Mexico since 1995 and in China since 1996. Beginning in 1995, we moved the labor-intensive sewing operation for our limited use/disposable protective clothing lines to these facilities. Our facilities and capabilities in China and Mexico provide access to a labor pool that is less expensive than that available in the U.S. and permits us to purchase certain raw materials at a lower cost than are available domestically. During FY25 and continuing into FY26, the Company was impacted by tariff costs on certain products imported from China. In addition, U.S. trade policy has undergone significant shifts under the Trump administration, including the imposition of new and expanded tariffs on key trading partners such as China, Vietnam, Canada, Mexico, and the European Union. These developments, along with potential retaliatory tariffs, have created increased uncertainty and cost pressures. In prior years, the Company has been able to pass along a portion of costs resulting from tariffs to its customers, but there is no guarantee that we will be able to successfully do so in the future.

During FY26, we expanded our product portfolio, geographic reach and services capabilities as part of our strategy to build a premier global fire services brand. However, our operations were impacted by external factors such as increases in freight costs, raw material inflation and ongoing supply-chain disruptions. In addition, we have experienced uncertainty in certain markets, certification timing delays and material flow challenges. These factors have negatively impacted our production efficiency, revenue timing and gross margins. We are continuing to implement initiatives to improve operational and manufacturing efficiencies, reduce inventory levels and prioritize liquidity and debt reduction.

We added manufacturing operations in Vietnam and India in fiscal 2019 to offset increasing manufacturing costs in China and further diversify our manufacturing capabilities. Our China operations will continue primarily manufacturing for the Chinese market and other markets where duty advantages exist. Manufacturing expansion is not only necessary to control rising costs, but also for Lakeland to achieve its growth objectives.

We have two U.S. based manufacturing locations through our acquisition of Veridian Limited in FY25. These facilities currently produce Veridian's brand of fire turnout gear and gloves, but they are in the process of being certified to produce Lakeland turnout gear for the U.S. market. They are also capable of producing Lakeland's woven and high-performance garments. In addition, as part of our broader strategy to expand our fire services platform, we completed the acquisitions of Arizona PPE and California PPE in FY26 that enhance our service capabilities in cleaning, inspection, repair, and rental of personal protective equipment.
Our net sales attributable to customers outside the U.S. were $111.0 million and $106.8 million for the fiscal years ended January 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

On September 15, 2025, the Company acquired 100% of U.S.-based California PPE Recon, Inc. ("California PPE") for a combination of approximately $2.4 million in cash consideration and 227,728 unregistered shares of the Company's common stock with an estimated fair value of $3.3 million at the date of acquisition, subject to post-closing adjustments and customary holdback provisions. Founded in 2022, California PPE is a leading and rapidly expanding UL-certified ISP in the California firefighting services market, one of the largest fire markets in the U.S. It also provides advanced decontamination, repair, and inspection of firefighting personal protective equipment, along with rental services and sales of cleaning detergents, extractors, and dryers.

On January 24, 2025, the Company issued 2,093,000 shares of its common stock in an underwritten offering at a price of $20.68 after an underwriting discount. After expenses the Company received approximately $46.2 million which was used to pay down the Company's revolving credit facility.

LHD is headquartered in Wesseling, Germany, with operations in Hong Kong and Australia.

(collectively, "Jolly") in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $9.0 million. The company is headquartered in Montebelluna, Italy, with manufacturing operations in Bucharest, Romania. Jolly provides a differentiated product portfolio through its continued investment in research and development and the use of modern materials and cutting-edge technologies in the production of its footwear.

headings: 客戶 – 我們的銷售主要透過經銷進行。截至2026年1月31日及2025年1月31日止會計年度，沒有任何單一客戶佔我們銷售額超過10%。
關於我們高階管理人員之資訊
paragraphs: 概要 – Lakeland Fire + Safety 是一家全球性公司，提供高品質的安全產品，用以保護世界各地的工作者、第一 responders 以及社區在最關鍵的情況下。本公司產品受嚴格的安全標準與規範所規範，用以保護穿戴者免於環境危害，或保護產品或過程免於穿戴者，應用於全球多種市場，包括化學、潔淨室、能源、消防服務、製造以及公共事業等領域。Lakeland 的產品組合包括消防員保護裝備與配件、高階化學防護服、有限使用/一次性防護服、耐用織布服裝、高性能 FR/AR 服裝以及高可見性服裝。於 2026 年 3 月 27 日，本公司將高性能 FR/AR 服裝與高可見性服裝系列出售給 National Safety Apparel。如需更多資訊，請參閱我們合併財務報表的附註 14。

Lakeland Fire + Safety 2026 財年反映持續進展，推動我們的策略，建立涵蓋 Fire Services 與 Industrial 產品線的全面性保護產品與服務組合。在該年度，我們完成兩項收購，擴充了我們在消防服裝上的先進去汙、檢查與維修服務能力，進一步強化了 Fire Services 平台。雖然我們認為目前已經擁有完整的全球頭到腳消防服務產品組合，但我們預期會持續推動策略，加速成長與毛利率，並持續聚焦於收購消防員出勤服裝產業。我們持續看到消防與工業領域的成長機會。我們已實現年年成長的營收，並透過最近的收購展現成功，這為我們的收購策略提供了信心，目前我們擁有充足的資金與靈活性來執行此策略。

本公司在重點產品類別與市場的強大市場地位，受到持續且增加的投資支撐，特別是在全球據點的擁有與運營，特別是擁有並運營自己的製造廠，收購補充本公司或產品以擴充與提升產品組合與/或地理客戶市場，並投資於全球各國的銷售與行銷資源。我們認為製造廠的擁有是建立韌性供應鏈與為客戶提供高品質產品的關鍵。擁有八個國家的九個製造據點，並從多個國家的多個供應商處取得核心原材料，使 Lakeland 具備優越的製造能力與供應鏈韌性，與那些使用外包商的競爭對手相比。此外，我們對提供客戶最佳等級的服務的關注，包括銷售團隊成員的戰略佈局。
Lakeland 承諾保護世界各地的工作者、第一 responders 以及社區，同時創造股東價值。我們企業戰略的關鍵要素包括：
• 建立以企業價值為導向的高績效文化， • 投資於高成長地理區域與產品類別，
• 透過產品與行銷提升，建立首選的全球消防員安全品牌，
• 透過產品開發、戰略價格方案、通路多元化與作業最佳化，推動高階化學與有限使用/一次性防護服的可持續成長，以及
• 收購提升 Lakeland 在重點市場競爭優勢的公司。
於 2025 年 9 月 15 日，本公司以現金約 4.1 百萬美元取得美國亞利桑那州 PPE Recon, Inc.（"Arizona PPE"）100% 的股權。Arizona PPE 於 2016 年成立，為亞利桑那州市場提供先進的防護服去汙、檢查與修復服務，並提供教育與訓練課程予消防部門及人員，協助其落實與遵守 NFPA 1851 指南，為 UL 認證的獨立服務供應商（"ISP"）。

於 2025 年 9 月 15 日，本公司以現金約 2.4 百萬美元及 227,728 張未註冊的本公司普通股股份（估計公平價值為 3.3 百萬美元）取得美國加利福尼亞州 PPE Recon, Inc.（"California PPE"）100% 的股權，此交易受交割後調整及慣例保留款條款約束。California PPE 於 2022 年成立，為美國加利福尼亞州消防服務市場中領先且快速成長的 UL 認證 ISP，為該市場最大之一。其亦提供先進的防護服去汙、修復與檢查服務，並提供租賃服務及清潔劑、萃取機與烘乾機的銷售。
於 2024 年 12 月 16 日，本公司以現金約 26.3 百萬美元取得美國 Veridian Limited（"Veridian"）的股權，此交易受交割後調整及慣例保留款條款約束。Veridian 於 1992 年成立，為消防員防護服裝的主要供應商，包括防火與救災服裝、手套與靴子，總部設於愛荷華州得梅因。

於 2024 年 7 月 1 日，本公司以現金交易取得 LHD Group Deutschland GmbH 及其在香港與澳洲子公司（合稱 "LHD"）的消防與救災業務。總交易金額為 14.8 百萬美元，扣除取得現金 1.5 百萬美元後，其中 15.5 百萬美元用以償還 LHD 的債務，0.8 百萬美元於交割時支付予賣方。LHD 為消防員出勤裝備、配件及個人防護裝備清潔、修復與維護的主要供應商，總部設於德國韋塞林格，並在香港與澳洲設有營運據點。
於 2024 年 2 月 5 日，本公司以現金交易取得義大利與羅馬尼亞的 Jolly Scarpe S.p.A. 及 Jolly Scarpe Romania S.R.L.（合稱 "Jolly"）的股權。總交易金額評估為 9.0 百萬美元。Jolly 為專業足部裝備的主要設計與製造商，服務於消防、軍事、警察與救災市場。該公司總部設於義大利蒙特貝洛納，製造業務設於羅馬尼亞布加勒斯特。

應報告分部 – 本公司根據 ASC 課題 280 "分部報告"，有七個產生營業收入的應報告地理分部：美國運營、其他外國、歐洲、墨西哥、亞洲、加拿大及拉丁美洲。分部報告內容請參閱本 10-K 表單 Part II Item 8 中的第 14 註 – 分部資訊。由於本公司合併財務報表以美金為單位，且許多業務在美國境外進行，匯率波動可能影響本公司營運成果與財務狀況，並可能影響不同會計期間的營運成果可比性。

paragraphs: 你應閱讀下列摘要，並與本表單 10-K 其他處出現的更詳細業務資訊及合併財務報表與相關附註一併參考。本文件可能包含某些根據 1995 年私人證券訴訟改革法案所定義的「前瞻性」資訊。此資訊涉及風險與不確定性。我們的實際結果可能與前瞻性陳述中所討論的結果有重大差異。在本表單 10-K 中，(a)「FY」指財務年度；例如，FY26 指 2026 年 1 月 31 日結止的財務年度，(b)「Q」指一個季度；例如，Q4 FY26 指 2026 年 1 月 31 日結止財務年度的第四季。

Lakeland Industries, Inc. 及其子公司，營業名稱為 "Lakeland Fire + Safety"（"Lakeland"、"本公司"、"我們"、"我們的" 或 "我們"），製造與銷售一整套防火服務及工業防護服裝與配件，用於工業與第一應變者市場。此外，我們也提供去汙、維修與租賃服務，以補強我們的防火服務產品線。我們的產品透過我們內建的銷售團隊、客戶服務部門及授權的獨立銷售代表，銷售至一個戰略性且選擇性的全球授權經銷商網路。我們的授權經銷商向各產業的最終用戶供應產品，包括整合型石油、化學/石化、汽車、運輸、鋼鐵、玻璃、建設、熔煉、潔淨室、清潔服務、製藥與高科技電子製造商，以及科學、醫療實驗室與電力產業。我們也供應聯邦、州與地方政府機構與部門，包括消防與執法部門、機場撞擊救災單位、國防部、國土安全部與疾病管制中心。國際上，我們根據不同國家與市場，直接銷售給最終用戶或工業經銷商。除了美國（U.S.）之外，銷售也進行至超過 50 個外國國家，其中大多數為中國、歐洲經濟共同體（"EEC"）、加拿大、智利、阿根廷、俄羅斯、哈薩克、哥倫比亞、墨西哥、厄瓜多、印度、烏拉圭、中東、東南亞、澳洲、香港與紐西蘭。
我們在 FY26 的淨銷售額為 192.6 百萬美元，在 FY25 的淨銷售額為 167.2 百萬美元。

我們自 1995 年起在墨西哥設有廠區，自 1996 年起在中國設有廠區。自 1995 年起，我們將勞動密集型的縫製作業，用於我們有限使用/一次性防護服產品線，移至這些廠區。我們在中國與墨西哥的廠區與能力，使我們能接觸到成本較低的勞動力，並讓我們能以較低的成本購買某些原材料，而這些原材料在國內可得性較高。在 FY25 年度及持續至 FY26 年度，本公司受到從中國進口產品的關稅成本影響。此外，美國貿易政策在特朗普政府時期經歷了顯著的變動，包括對關鍵貿易夥伴如中國、越南、加拿大、墨西哥與歐盟施加新的及擴大的關稅。這些發展，加上潛在的報復性關稅，已造成增加的不確定性與成本壓力。在過去幾年，本公司已能將部分因關稅產生的成本轉嫁給客戶，但無法保證我們未來能成功做到這一點。
在 FY26 年度，我們擴充了產品組合、地理範圍與服務能力，作為我們建立首屈一指全球防火服務品牌的策略之一。然而，我們的營運受到外部因素的影響，例如運輸成本增加、原材料通貨膨脹與持續的供應鏈中斷。此外，我們經歷了某些市場的不確定性、認證時間延遲與物料流動困難。這些因素已對我們的生產效率、收入時點與毛利率造成負面影響。我們持續實施方案以提高營運與製造效率、降低存貨水準並優先處理流動性與債務減少。
我們在財務年度 2019 年增加了越南與印度的製造業務，以抵銷中國製造成本的增加，並進一步分散製造能力。我們的中國業務將繼續主要製造中國市場及其他有關稅優勢的市場。製造擴張不僅是控制成本上升的必要措施，也是 Lakeland 達成成長目標的必要條件。

我們透過 FY25 年收購 Veridian Limited，在美國設有兩個製造廠區。這些廠區目前生產 Veridian 的防火作業服與手套品牌，但正在進行認證程序，以生產美國市場的 Lakeland 防火作業服。這些廠區也具備生產 Lakeland 的織布與高性能服裝的能力。此外，作為我們擴展防火服務平台的廣泛策略之一，我們在 FY26 年完成了 Arizona PPE 與 California PPE 的收購，這些收購增強了我們在個人防護裝備清潔、檢查、維修與租賃服務的能力。
我們在 2026 年 1 月 31 日結止財務年度，來自美國以外客戶的淨銷售額為 111.0 百萬美元，而在 2025 年 1 月 31 日結止財務年度為 106.8 百萬美元。

於 2025 年 9 月 15 日，本公司以現金約 4.1 百萬美元取得美國亞利桑那州 PPE Recon, Inc.（"Arizona PPE"）100% 的股權，此交易需經交割後調整及慣常的保留款條款。Arizona PPE 於 2016 年成立，為亞利桑那州市場領先的 UL 認證獨立服務供應商（"ISP"），專門執行消防服裝的高階去汙、檢查與維修服務，同時也提供教育與訓練課程給消防部門及人員，協助他們落實並遵守 NFPA 1851 指南。

於 2025 年 9 月 15 日，本公司以現金約 2.4 百萬美元及 227,728 張未註冊的本公司普通股股份（估計於取得日的公平價值為 3.3 百萬美元）取得美國加利福尼亞州 PPE Recon, Inc.（"California PPE"）100% 的股權，此交易需經交割後調整及慣常的保留款條款。California PPE 於 2022 年成立，為美國加利福尼亞州消防服務市場領先且快速成長的 UL 認證 ISP，為美國最大消防市場之一。該公司也提供高階去汙、維修與檢查消防個人防護裝備，並提供租賃服務及清潔劑、萃取機與烘乾機的銷售。
於 2025 年 1 月 24 日，本公司發行 2,093,000 張普通股股份，透過承銷方式以每股 20.68 美元發行，扣除承銷折扣後，本公司收到約 46.2 百萬美元，此金額用以償還本公司週轉信用貸款。
於 2024 年 12 月 16 日，本公司以現金約 26.3 百萬美元取得美國 Veridian Limited，此交易需經交割後調整及慣常的保留款條款。Veridian 於 1992 年成立，為消防員防護服裝的領先供應商，包括消防與救援服裝、手套與靴子，總部設於愛荷華州得梅因。

於 2024 年 7 月 1 日，本公司以全現金交易取得 LHD Group Deutschland GmbH 及其在香港與澳洲的子公司（合稱 "LHD"）的消防與救援業務。總交易金額為 14.8 百萬美元，扣除取得現金 1.5 百萬美元後，其中 15.5 百萬美元用以償還 LHD 的債務，0.8 百萬美元於交割時支付給賣方。LHD 為消防員出勤裝備、配件及個人防護裝備清潔、維修與保養的領先供應商，總部設於德國韋塞林格，並在香港與澳洲設有營運據點。

於 2024 年 2 月 5 日，本公司以全現金交易取得義大利與羅馬尼亞的 Jolly Scarpe S.p.A. 及 Jolly Scarpe Romania S.R.L.（合稱 "Jolly"），總價值約 9.0 百萬美元。Jolly 為專業足部裝備的領先設計與製造商，服務於消防、軍事、警察與救援市場。該公司總部設於義大利蒙特貝洛納，製造業務設於羅馬尼亞布加勒斯特。Jolly 透過持續投資於研究與發展，以及在製造足部裝備時使用現代材料與尖端科技，提供差異化的產品組合。

headings: 與本公司業務及產業相關之風險
本公司因國際製造業務而面臨風險，包括因國際貿易環境近期發展所產生之風險，例如進口關稅增加。
恐怖攻擊或其他地緣政治危機可能對本公司之國內及/或國際營運造成負面影響。
本公司營運成果可能因季度而異。
供應鏈、製造或配送業務中斷，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
氣候變遷及其他永續性議題可能對本公司業務及營運造成不利影響。
疫情或疾病爆發，例如 COVID-19，可能導致不利之經濟或市場條件，進而影響需求模式及/或幹擾全球供應鏈及製造業務。
由於本公司與許多客戶並無長期契約，因此必須預估客戶需求，若預估錯誤，可能對本公司存貨水準及淨銷售額造成負面影響。
我們所競爭的市場具有高度競爭性，且部分競爭對手擁有較我們更優越的財務及其他資源。
我們的營運在很大程度上依賴關鍵人員。
科技變革可能對我們產品的銷售及營運表現產生負面影響。
網路安全事件可能幹擾營運，導致關鍵及機密資訊遺失，並對我們的聲譽及營運結果造成不利影響。
我們的成功在一定程度上取決於專有技術，若我們未能成功取得或執行智慧財產權權利，將可能影響我們的競爭地位。
我們若無法成功識別、完成並整合現有及未來的併購與戰略投資，或無法實現預期的成本節省及其他好處，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們正在實施新的企業資源規劃系統，系統實施過程中的挑戰或進一步延誤，可能影響我們對財務報導的內部控制、營運及業務。
我們過去已認列減損費用，未來可能仍需認列額外的減損費用，包括 goodwill 及其他無形資產。
財務風險
我們的營運成果可能因外幣匯率波動而受到負面影響。
我們信貸協議中的約束條款可能限制我們的財務與營運彈性。
我們可能需要額外資金，若無法取得這些資金，我們可能無法按計畫擴張或營運業務。
法律與法規風險
我們因國際營運而受某些美國與外國反貪污法律及其他法律與法規的約束。
我們受各種美國與外國稅法的約束，這些法律若因企業稅收或稅務爭議解決而有所變更，可能對我們的營運成果造成負面影響。
我們可能面臨產品責任索賠，且保險覆蓋範圍可能不足或無法取得以覆蓋這些索賠。
paragraphs: 您在投資本公司普通股前應謹慎考慮下列風險。下列所描述的風險與不確定性為本公司已識別為重要的風險，但並非本公司可能面臨的唯一風險。如果下列所提及的任何事件實際發生，將可能使本公司業務、財務狀況、流動性及營運成果受損。在這種情況下，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。此外，下列所討論的風險包含前瞻性陳述，而本公司實際結果可能與前瞻性陳述中所討論的結果有顯著差異。請參閱標題為「與前瞻性陳述相關之資訊」的章節，以瞭解這些陳述及其限制。您也應參考本Form 10-K及其他資訊，以及本公司所引用入本Form 10-K之文件，包括本公司合併財務報表及相關附註。

因為我們大多數產品是在中國、越南、墨西哥、阿根廷、紐西蘭、羅馬尼亞及印度設有廠區所製造，因此我們的業務面臨國際營運的風險。這些風險包括腐敗、戰爭、國際恐怖主義、民變、政治不穩定、貿易戰、政府活動如邊境稅及條約重新談判，以及合同與財產權被剝奪及貨幣價值變動對營運造成的不利影響。根據中國與美國之間複雜的關係，存在內在風險，即政治、外交、軍事或其他事件可能導致業務中斷，包括對公司的增加監管執法、關稅、貿易禁運及出口限制。

近年來，美國對進口至美國的各種產品課徵關稅。這些關稅已導致，並可能繼續引發受影響國家的報復行動，包括對美國課徵關稅。在現任政府任內，貿易政策成為重點，重新審視與中國的貿易關係，並努力重新談判或退出關鍵協議，例如美國-墨西哥-加拿大協議（USMCA）。此轉變包括引入額外關稅，包括針對墨西哥、加拿大、中國、越南、歐盟及印度商品的關稅，以及針對被視為對美國國家安全至關重要的產業的投資限制與制裁。某些外國政府，例如中國、加拿大、墨西哥及歐盟，已實施或正在考慮對某些美國商品課徵貿易制裁，並拒絕美國公司取得關鍵原材料的存取權。

我們無法預測增加關稅的程度與持續時間，以及對總體經濟狀況及本公司業務的影響，這些影響尚不確定，並取決於多種因素，例如美國與受影響國家之間的談判、其他國家或地區的反應、可能給予的豁免或排除、替代供應來源的可得性與成本，以及受影響市場對我們產品的需求。例如，在2025年4月宣佈對來自越南進口商品課徵46%的總體關稅後，美國與越南政府宣佈兩國之間的貿易協議，對所有進口至美國的越南商品課徵20%關稅，該協議自2025年8月7日起生效。2026年2月20日，美國最高法院作出裁決，廢除根據國際緊急經濟權力法（"IEEPA"）所課徵的某些關稅，但未處理根據IEEPA所支付關稅的潛在退款問題。有關這些關稅的退款是否可得、時間及金額，仍極為不確定，並受進一步法律、監管及行政發展的影響。在最高法院裁決後，特朗普政府立即根據1974年貿易法第122條，課徵新的全球關稅，該條款允許課徵最高15%的關稅，持續至多150天，並表示有意考慮其他法律途徑課徵關稅。

我們的業務已因IEEPA關稅而受到負面影響，未來也可能因這快速演變的關稅情況及由此產生的經濟不確定性而受到負面影響。關稅提高了我們產品的成本，以及製造這些產品所需的零組件與原材料的成本。這些成本增加不利於我們產品的毛利率。關稅也提高了我們產品的客戶成本，使其競爭力下降，並導致消費者需求減少。國家也可能採用其他措施，例如對商品、技術或數據的進口或出口進行管制，這些措施可能對本公司營運及供應鏈造成不利影響，並限制本公司提供設計的產品與服務的能力。這些措施可能要求我們採取各種行動，包括更換供應商、將某些產品的生產轉移到關稅較低的國家，以及重新調整業務關係。根據新的或變更的貿易限制調整我們的營運可能昂貴、耗時且幹擾營運，同時也會分散管理層的注意力。這些限制已於過去被宣佈、修改、暫停、恢復或廢止，且往往沒有事先通知，我們可能無法有效緩解所有這些措施的負面影響。貿易及其他國際爭議的不確定性已對消費者信心與支出產生負面影響，我們無法預測這種不確定性可能持續多久。這些事件已導致客戶需求減少，額外的關稅政策可能加劇這些影響，提高我們產品與服務的成本，或以其他方式對我們客戶與供應商的業務與營運成果產生重大負面影響，進而進一步對我們的財務表現與成長前景產生負面影響。
我們的全球營運易受全球事件影響，包括戰爭或恐怖活動、國際衝突、政治不穩定及自然災害。上述任何事件的發生或持續，都可能對我們的營運成果與財務狀況產生不利影響。
